title: Talk-show bands and the Palace's guest hosts
summary: Dance and Edison discuss the role of Johnny Carson's band, then Edison lists stars who hosted the Palace.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, what I never understand about Carson's show is what does he have that band for? Does that play during the ads?
Yes, oh yes.
That plays for the audience.
Yes.
Because it almost seems a --
And when they have singers come on the show, they back the singers, you know, like -- and the band is a part of the show now.
Yeah.
Everybody expects to hear that band, you know.
Well, it just seems rather ridiculous to keep a full band and you never get to hear them.
Yeah, well, it's some work for the musicians.
Oh, yes, that's good. But you know --
The audience on there,they look forward to hearing that band. They've got a good band.
That's what it is.
They've got a good band, fantastic band. But that Hollywood Palace thing was --
And when you --

-- good. Oh, we had fiddles, we had everything, because we had to play for dancers. We had to play -- it was like a Roxy theater, only we had a big artist -- a star would emcee the show every week, you know, like, let's see. Oh, I mentioned Douglas Fairbanks. Omar Sharif, he would be the emcee. Then Pearl Bailey would be the emcee one week. Lena Horne would be the emcee one week.
And you had to play every kind of music.
All kinds of music because we had acts that come out of the circus acts, you know, and it was like a vaudeville show.
Well, --
And it was a fantastic show.
